title: Paints and Salt
summary: The pan crew has cut the season's first ochre — four sacks of the deep rust-red that makes a garage a garage. Brinemaster Ogo wants it weighed, waxed and walked to Ketch's paint bench before someone reclassifies it as a luxury. There may be a fifth sack. There is officially no fifth sack.

objectives.label: Lift the ochre sacks from the pan crew's dig flap
Weigh and wax-seal the pigment at the exchange scale
Deliver the sealed ochre to Ketch's paint bench

offer.text: Courier Varga. Sit— no, don't. Pigment work. The pan crew cut the season's first ochre this morning, the deep rust-red, and every hour it sits unmanifested some clerk gets ideas. Four sacks, dig flap at the old pan, to my scale, then to that garage you frequent.

A word on wax: cargo class lives in the colour band, courier. Ochre band means sealed against damp, sand and amateur opinions. Break a seal wrong and you can unmarry someone — it's in the manual. Read the manual. The manual is a perk of employment.

accept.text: Four sacks of dirt, weighed by a soul-scale, walked three hundred metres. What's the catch? There's a catch with you. The catch has a catch.

No catch. A rounding, let us say. If Sister Counterweight's scale reads a weight that disagrees with your manifest, you will hear me applauding her instrument, and you will say nothing, because wax is thicker than paperwork. Off you go.
Counterweight to the courier now riding to the pan. The scale has been pre-informed. It is humming a little song that sounds like 'five'. That is all.

complete.text: For the record: four sacks, wax-sealed, ochre band, correctly manifested. There was also a gift. Gifts under two kilos, carried with intent, are outside tariff — the Guild is firm on this, I checked twice. The pan crew gives well. I have weighed presents that were only debts wearing ribbon. Not this one.

Hold on — hold on. Five sacks. Four Guild, one... oh, those diggers. Thirty years they remember an old resin recipe I taught a season-hand. Look at this red, kid. Violet undertone, like a canyon worrying about something. This isn't pigment, it's a reunion.

Ogo, exchange band. A satisfactory transaction all round: the Guild measured pigment, the garage received paint, and nobody anywhere was seen to be generous. Reputations intact. You've a steady hand with a scale-adjacent matter, Varga. Dull work, honestly done — the Guild's highest compliment. There's a pamphlet. I've billed you for it.
